meta.title: Fleetwright — Reliable Browser Operations
meta.description: Authorized browser workflows with durable execution, human approval, scoped MCP access and verifiable recovery.

headline: Browser Operations
With Evidence
hero.subhead: Supervise authorized workflows from one control plane. Approve exact actions, recover interrupted work and inspect the evidence behind every outcome.
hero.statsCaption: Owned-workflow verification: 200 competitors / 10,000 jobs; browser capacity measured separately through 32 contexts.

problem.text: Several workers see the same opportunity. One acts, then dies before recording the answer. Without durable intent and destination evidence, the next worker can repeat an action that already succeeded.

claimRace.title: One authority. Verifiable outcomes.
claimRace.fallbackNote: Interactive 3D view unavailable — the steps below describe the same sequence.

steps.title: A watcher sees the load
steps.body: Watchers read the board's JSON responses, not the DOM, and publish a DETECTED event with a seen_at timestamp.

steps.title: Every matching actor races
steps.body: Filters route the job to pre-warmed actors whose sessions are already logged in. Redis gives a fast first filter — never the final word.

steps.title: Postgres picks one winner
steps.body: INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on (tenant_id, target_job_key). The database's unique key decides. Everyone else gets nothing to act on.

steps.title: A fencing token guards the click
steps.body: The lease carries a monotonic token. A worker that paused past its lease is rejected by the database clock, not its own.

steps.title: Confirmed — or reconciled, never retried blind
steps.body: A crash mid-action becomes UNKNOWN. Reconciliation checks destination receipts. Insufficient evidence leaves the outcome unresolved for operator review.

workers.title: Coordinate the complete workflow.

cards.title: Claim worker
cards.body: Warm browser sessions, fenced database leases and receipt reconciliation coordinate freight actions across workers.
points: Unique claims and current fenced leases

cards.title: Crawler · planned
cards.body: Future authorized crawling with domain budgets, extraction contracts and data-quality checks.
points: SSRF and egress controls required before release

cards.title: Agent supervision
cards.body: Codex and Claude connect through scoped MCP tools to propose jobs, inspect progress and export evidence. Human approval remains in the owner console.
points: Approval bound to the exact action
Unknown outcomes are never blindly retried

workers.note: Panels use reference sequences to explain behavior. Live jobs and owner approvals are available in the console. The crawler and standalone agent interface remain planned.

latency.title: Six timestamps. No averaged-away excuses.
latency.note: Every claim is stamped at each stage. Reports split publish→detect from detect→action, with p50 / p95 / p99 per stage.

stages.label: Published
stages.body: Ground truth from the board's own event log.

stages.label: Queued
stages.body: Filters matched; the job enters the cell's stream.

stages.label: Leased
stages.body: Postgres grants the single lease and its fencing token.

stages.label: Act sent
stages.body: The warm page clicks, or the session's HTTP action fires.

stages.label: Confirmed
stages.body: The board confirms the booking; the audit log closes the loop.

cells.title: Bound failure by execution cell.
cells.body: The freight engine routes tenants to execution cells. This view explains the routing design; the public deployment remains one host, and general workflow cell assignment is future work.
cells.liveRegionFailed: Routing view: cell A is unavailable; the target topology assigns its tenants to cell B.
cells.liveRegionRestored: Routing view: cell A is available again.

guardrails.title: Strict by default.

items.title: MFA for every operator
items.body: TOTP enforced; argon2id hashing; RBAC checked server-side on every endpoint.

items.title: Tenant isolation in the database
items.body: Tenant content tables use forced PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, with isolation tests.

items.title: Append-only audit log
items.body: Every mutation and every claim action is recorded.

items.title: No third-party captcha defeat
items.body: Owned verification challenges are separate from third-party access controls. Other destinations require permission and human challenge handling.

items.title: US + EU law register
items.body: Authorization, privacy, AI transparency and software-security obligations reviewed for each deployment and jurisdiction.

items.title: Credential redaction
items.body: Logging filters redact recognized credentials and codes; regression tests exercise the supported formats. Raw browser artifacts remain private.

guardrails.note: Implemented controls and remaining hardening work are documented publicly with their verification boundaries.

title: Inspect The Fleet
Review The Evidence
closing.body: Inspect the live freight engine, review approved browser workflows and investigate outcomes from one console.

footer.note: Fleetwright operates owned freight and maintenance workflows. External destinations require explicit authorization. Future capacity and availability milestones are documented in the roadmap.
